svg.title: M12: Typed evidence validation and coherent assessment
svg.desc: Typed proposals are checked for source spans, authorized scope and specific source authority. They remain candidates, become verified for a precise assertion or are rejected with a reason. Accepted changes publish a new input revision, recalculate affected results and produce a consistent case manifest.

g.text: M12 / EVIDENCE VALIDATION / PROPOSED HOST LOGIC
Verify a precise assertion. Publish a consistent case.
A verified quote, relationship and operational fact each establish different things.

g.title: A model proposal carries a source version, span and typed assertion
g.text: M11 proposal: note N-17 reports a retry of attempt A-004
Source version + quoted span + assertion kind + proposed endpoints + explicit uncertainty

g.title: The host checks the proposed evidence
Schema and span, scope and relation, authority and corroboration are separate checks
g.text: IDs and relation names prove no authority.

g.title: Each proposal receives a specific outcome and reason
Missing or ambiguous support remains candidate
g.text: Keep the gap; exclude from proof.

g.title: Verification applies only to the exact typed proposition
g.text: Keep its exact authority and scope.

g.title: Rejection means the proposal failed a check, not necessarily that its claim is false
Acceptance publishes an immutable input revision
Accepted changes trigger affected control and claim reassessment
g.text: Recompute affected runs, windows and objectives.

g.title: One manifest binds the case to consistent inputs and assessments
Case source, accepted inputs, assessments and explanation must agree
g.text: No old explanation attached to changed numbers.

g.title: Claim composition uses required objective-level results for a compatible declared scope
g.text: C-FM-01: compose the required branches for the declared scope.
Apply each objective's allowance. Preserve violations and unknowns. Do not average controls.
Three green assessments from incompatible runs, windows or rule versions do not establish one claim.
